trigger: A reader takes 'the total never exceeds the budget' and the header's silence on the per-entry cap as the whole memory story
summary: Comments claimed the total never exceeds the budget (true only for RETAINED entries; peak is retained plus validators in flight, with no single-flight), and the class header, constructor comment and 'never cached' line did not mention the 32 MiB per-entry cap added in 90fd7854d. Also raised by: docs-writer, security-guardian.
classification_rationale: comment contradicts the admission and peak-memory behaviour

summary: Header, cap constant and kPatternMaxMem comments now say retained total vs peak, document max_entry_bytes in all three places and state the rebuild-on-every-call trade (63770a71d). The cost figures added in that commit were wrong at -O2 and are dropped in e4ddf2ae9. Re-reviewed at 90fd7854d..63770a71d by docs-writer, sre, cpp-safety, quality-engineer: closed.

trigger: Concurrent execute calls against a definition whose validator exceeds the 32 MiB per-entry cap, or against more than four just-under-cap definitions rotating through the budget
summary: An entry that is not retained is rebuilt on every call and, with no single-flight, each concurrent caller builds and holds its own copy; peak memory is the retained total plus in-flight validators (pool of 264 workers by default). Measured: preparing a 128-pattern schema costs sub-millisecond for trivial patterns and about 11 ms for [a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64} at -O2 on one host (cpp-safety measured 0.74 ms for a different shape: cost depends on the pattern); the retained estimate is 2x or more above measured heap in every shape tried (ratios 0.01-0.49). Also raised by: security-guardian.
classification_rationale: bounded by the pool, needs InstructionDefinition:Write plus Execution:Execute

summary: Trade-off documented (63770a71d). The mechanism (single-flight or an in-flight map covering over-cap results, hit/miss/rebuild/eviction counters and a retained-bytes gauge, a measured in-flight ceiling, CPU re-timing at pool concurrency) is the remaining scope of existing issue #5562 and the precondition for the shared execute_definition() gate slice (Fable-reviewed sequence, project notes).

trigger: A holder of InstructionDefinition:Write plants a 128-pattern schema (estimated 64 MiB, inside the 128 MiB budget)
summary: One hostile entry evicted the whole ~27 MiB shipped catalogue in a single insert. Fixed in 90fd7854d with a 32 MiB per-entry admission cap; residual: 3-4 distinct just-under-cap (63 pattern) definitions can still rotate the catalogue out (no per-definition fairness), accepted and pinned by a test. Also raised by: sre, security-guardian.

Per-entry cap commit 90fd7854d with tests (hostile schemas served but never retained; per-entry boundary; just-under-cap rotation) and mutation proofs; reviewed by security-guardian, sre, architect, cpp-safety, quality-engineer: no memory-exhaustion path found (estimate/real ratio at most 0.49).

trigger: A refactor of the weight formula, the cap, the eviction loop or the racy insert path
summary: Gaps: no items-enum weight assertion, per-entry cap boundary and bytes() after concurrency unpinned, no multi-entry eviction case, the concurrent double-count mutant red only 5 runs in 6, a tautological admitted==4 check. Also raised by: cpp-safety.

Added the items-enum weight, cap boundary, bytes() after concurrency, multi-eviction and just-under-cap tests (63770a71d); start gate with an RAII OpenGate makes the double-count mutant red 10 of 10 runs and the tautology is removed (e4ddf2ae9). Mutants for each pin were red then restored.
